title: se implementation scratchpad - lynx bank
content:
Context/goal:
- Implementation scratchpad for Lynx Bank private deployment (POC -> Prod).
- Primary asks: VPC-based private control plane, KMS/HSM integration, SSO (SAML), restricted egress, SLA for latency <= 120ms p50 for chat endpoint.

Meeting notes (2026-02-15 kickoff):
- Attendees: Samira, Evan, Priya (Redwood), Mark H. (Lynx infra), Leah P. (Lynx security).
- Lynx will start with 2-node POC in their VPC, want path to Dedicated (reserved) after approval.
- Data flow: requests -> Lynx API Gateway -> private Redwood control plane (peered) -> serving nodes in Lynx VPC. No public internet egress for inference.

Quick checklist (POC):
[ ] final infra diagram for VPC peering and cross-account roles
[ ] confirm KMS key policy and key rotation window (customer wants HSM backed keys)
[ ] SAML metadata exchange (IdP endpoint, cert)
[ ] network rules: CIDR ranges to allow (see notes)
[ ] sizing recommendation for initial POC (GPUs + RAM)
[ ] plan for logs/metrics transfer (internal-only syslog sink)
[ ] run smoke test harness and evaluation prompt set

Configuration notes / suggestions:
- Model: start with rwd-3b-8bit (recommended for cost/latency tradeoff) — fallback to rwd-7b-q4 when quality needed.
- Serving: 2x A10G (or 4x T4) equivalent for POC to support 20 concurrent sessions with KV cache enabled. Recommend A10G if Lynx has budget.
- Storage: S3-compatible bucket inside their VPC for model artifacts; object lifecycle not public. Prefix: s3://lynx-redwood/models/prod/
- KMS: customer uses AWS CloudHSM; need IAM role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Lynx-Redwood-KMS-Access. Ask Lynx to provide key alias and policy.
- Networking: open outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints only (IP list to be provided). Ports: 443 (control plane), 22 only for scheduled maint (jumpbox), 9090 for internal metrics (optional behind tunnel).
- SSO: SAML 2.0 — request IdP metadata, ACS URL will be provided by Redwood private control plane.
- Audit logs: send to customer CloudWatch Logs or to S3 with SSE-KMS using customer key.

Integration/ops runbook snippets (notes to self):
- Install helm chart: redwood/private-control-plane with values:
  - replicaCount: 2
  - nodeSelector.gpu: "true"
  - resources.requests.gpu: 2
  - persistence.modelBucket: "s3://lynx-redwood/models/prod"
  - kms.provider: "aws-cloudhsm"
  - tls.secretName: "lynx-redwood-tls"
- Post-install: run ./scripts/verify-smoke.sh --endpoint <internal-endpoint> --key <test-api-key>
- Smoke tests: latency, concurrency, token-usage, KV-cache correctness, and quality regression against saved eval set (lynx-eval-2026-02).

Open questions / blockers:
- Lynx security asked for no external logging. Need to confirm if Redwood agent can run in customer VPC and ship metrics via mTLS to their metrics collector.
- Does Lynx require PCI-like controls? They said "financial controls" but need clear checklist.
- HSM access timing: when can they provide signing certificate?

Next steps (this week):
- [ ] Send infra diagram draft to Mark (Samira) by 2026-02-18.
- [ ] Get SAML metadata and KMS alias from Leah by 2026-02-20.
- [ ] Provision POC k8s cluster with 2 A10G nodes (Evan).
- [ ] Create GitHub PR with helm values and secrets template (Jared).
- [ ] Schedule smoke run with Lynx (Priya) for 2026-02-25.

Notes to self: keep prompts and eval set small for POC (focus on latency/throughput). Save any customer-provided sample data under secure path and mark as sensitive. Use feature-flag to enable/disable model quantization in the chart.

Recent edits (2026-03-02):
- Updated recommended GPU to A10G after budget discussion (Mark).
- Added linked artifacts PR and Jira ticket.

-- end of scratchpad --
